[USER] User inquired about a term to describe a probability curve being generated rather than a single prediction.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The term used to describe a probability curve generated by a machine learning model is "probability distribution".  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A probability distribution is a function that describes the likelihood of different outcomes of a random event.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In binary classification problems, a machine learning model can generate a probability distribution over the two possible classes (e.g., 0 and 1).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The probability distribution gives the probabilities of the input belonging to each class.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] In regression problems, a machine learning model can generate a probability distribution over the possible values of the output variable.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The term "probability distribution" is used to describe the output of a machine learning model that generates a curve of probabilities over the possible outcomes instead of a single prediction.
